verification.independent_mask_assignment_check: Twelve cases selected by the first two alphabetical IDs within each of six domains; all 360 method-condition predictions independently reconstructed from packed masks, common IDs reconstructed from geometry/digest, semantic Hungarian IoU assignments rederived at both thresholds; exact agreement with producer results.

primary_common_wrapper_result.interpretation: No support for higher correct identity continuity than DBSCAN or NMS. The primary case-bootstrap estimate favors DBSCAN; that inferiority inference is not robust to category-cluster resampling. The NMS interval spans zero and does not establish equivalence.

scope_completeness.family_comparisons: All six HPID-minus-baseline contrasts at IoU .25 have 99.1666667% multiplicity-adjusted intervals spanning zero.
scope_completeness.secondary_threshold: IoU .50 has 55 common GT parts in 43 eligible cases; it is secondary, not a substitute primary endpoint.
scope_completeness.sensitivity: Pairwise common-target cohorts, pooled-target weighting, category-cluster bootstrap, every individual condition, native IDs and all-GT guardrails are retained in full.

native_id_diagnostic.finding: The native-ID secondary analysis also does not establish HPID superiority. Both adjusted paired intervals span zero.
native_id_diagnostic.what_common_wrapper_tests: Applying one visible-mask semantic/rank wrapper to all outputs removes a naming-rule advantage and estimates the comparative continuity of correct output instances under that fixed wrapper.
native_id_diagnostic.what_common_wrapper_does_not_test: It removes HPID's candidate-identity and parent-relative ID naming rules, so it does not isolate the potential value of HPID's full native identity contract, provenance, hierarchy or software package semantics.
native_id_diagnostic.what_native_comparison_tests: It compares each method together with its own ID rule: HPID's native hierarchical IDs versus deterministic baseline semantic/side/rank IDs. This is a complete-package diagnostic, not a causal estimate of the fusion algorithm alone.
native_id_diagnostic.combined_boundary: The common-wrapper result cannot by itself establish that the whole identity-contract contribution is valueless. However, neither this comparison nor the native-ID diagnostic provides evidence that HPID correctly preserves identities better than the tested baselines. No stability-superiority claim should be inserted.

perturbation_effectiveness.note: Predeclared round(0.10*N) removes zero proposals in small candidate sets. Retain these cases but disclose the dose discretization; their unchanged outputs do not independently demonstrate robustness. No outcome-driven change to perturbation dose is justified.

document_boundaries: These are post-hoc controlled perturbations of a previously analyzed 226-image cohort, not a fresh independent validation set.
Root, score and candidate-list inputs vary; image acquisition, semantic proposal generation and full-image detection are not rerun.
Persistent correct part lookup under these synthetic changes is measured; cross-frame tracking, real occluded-input identity recovery, human editing time and safety are not measured.

The original protocol limitations field retained root-only wording despite correctly listing all three families elsewhere. Disclose this as a documentation omission; do not silently revise or hash-replace the frozen protocol.
Main and secondary comparison families are explicitly separated. Individual descriptive 95% intervals across all exploratory metrics do not support a familywise-controlled superiority claim.
The original conclusion about an exported, inspectable identity contract remains an architectural claim. Comparative task benefits require additional successful evidence rather than a wording change.
